messages:
OpsBot: ALERT triggered: cont-batch scheduler p99 spike > 2s in streaming path in us-west-2 (service: runtime-gateway). Paging oncall.
Maya: I'm on it. seeing elevated p99 on streaming tail tokens, p95 still mostly okay. paging next badge.
Jamal: grabbing logs now, can you dump latest scheduler metrics? suspect mixed-seqlen amplification.
Maya: posting quick graphs — p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 2.3s, streaming stalls reported by customers (websocket timeouts). SLOs: p95 < 400ms, p99 < 1s so we're breaching p99.
Li: I see KV-cache churn around the same time, a bunch of new long-seq requests spiked. batch sizes jumped to 128 for some workers.
Maya: reproducible pattern: when a long-seq request enters a hot shard it delays many short streaming reqs.
Jamal: can we enable preemptive-shed on cont-batch to favor streaming paths? quick patch: lower `batch_scheduler.max_batch_size` from 128 -> 32 for streaming workers.
Alex: I'm in infra console. rolling a targeted config to runtime-pool-usw2-streaming-canary. Patch command:
```
# patch scheduler config for pool
rtctl update-pool --pool runtime-pool-usw2-streaming --set batch_scheduler.max_batch_size=32 --set batch_scheduler.preemptive=true
```
Maya: doing canary now on 2 nodes.
SRE-Bot: DEPLOY START runtime-pool-usw2-streaming CANARY by Alex @ 5991234578
Maya: also enabling `fair_share.enable_mixedlen_preemption=true` in canary — should reduce starvation of short requests.
Li: logs from node-7 show long requests pinning KV cache; evicting old KV shards helps short requests get through. Can we trigger a KV eviction TTL bump for streaming pool? small risk but temporary.
Jamal: +1, do it only on canary first.
Alex: running eviction command on canary nodes:
```
rtctl kv-evict --pool runtime-pool-usw2-streaming --age-threshold 300s --dry-run=false
```
Maya: canary metrics ~ 60s in: p99 down from 2.3s -> 900ms, p95 down to ~250ms. Not fully stable but trending better.
CustomerSuccess: we have 3 customers reporting interactive stalls (session ids attached). Not yet customer-facing incident page but CS notified.
Maya: notifying product + CS. Adding a temporary traffic steering rule to route heavy-long requests to dedicated batch pool (non-streaming) as fallback.
Jamal: route applied via gateway filter chain: if request.seqlen > 1024 -> route=dedicated-batch-usw2. Command:
```
api-gw patch-rule --if 'ctx.request.meta.seq_len > 1024' --route dedicated-batch-usw2 --priority 50
```
Maya: rule live at 5991234599. initial telemetry shows ~8% of streaming traffic offloaded.
Li: after offload, p99 hit ~720ms across streaming pool, p95 ~220ms. Streaming timeouts reduced significantly.
Maya: good. I'll keep canary running for 15m and then roll to remaining streaming nodes if stable.
Anne: I'm next oncall at 6000000000 — I'll take handoff in 10m. what are open action items to pass along?
Maya: handoff checklist:
- Monitor p99/p95 for next 30m, if p99 < 1s for 10m -> keep config and schedule postmortem
- If p99 creeps back above 1s -> revert traffic rule and re-enable wider eviction + consider draining node hotspots
- Follow up with eng-runtime to implement finer-grained batching strategy: `max_batch_size` per-seqlen-class and streaming-priority queues
- Postmortem owner: Jamal
- Notify affected customers with timeline and mitigation note (CS)
Jamal: I'll own the postmortem. initial hypothesis: mixed-seq arrival + greedy packer + KV hot-sharding => batching amplification. We'll need a test harness to simulate mixedlen tails.
Maya: adding temporary guard rails: `batch_scheduler.max_wait_ms=10` (was 40) on streaming pool to reduce wait amplification.
SRE-Bot: CONFIG PATCH applied by Maya @ 5991234615: batch_scheduler.max_wait_ms=10
Maya: system metrics steady for 5m. p99 ~ 650-800ms. streaming stalls reported cleared by CS. marking mitigation as successful for now.
CustomerSuccess: updated customers with interim report and ETA for postmortem.
Anne: acknowledged, will pick up monitoring and escalation if it regresses. please paste the exact config diffs for the postmortem.
Jamal: diffs:
- batch_scheduler.max_batch_size: 128 -> 32 (streaming pool)
- batch_scheduler.preemptive: false -> true
- batch_scheduler.max_wait_ms: 40 -> 10
- fair_share.enable_mixedlen_preemption: false -> true
- gateway rule: seq_len > 1024 -> dedicated-batch-usw2 (priority 50)
- KV eviction: age-threshold 300s triggered on streaming canary
Maya: will attach metrics dashboards (p95/p99, batch sizes histogram, seq_len distribution) to the incident thread.
Anne: thanks — handover complete. I'll update status if anything changes. good job team :thumbsup!
OpsBot: INCIDENT HANDOFF logged. new oncall: Anne. incident state -> monitoring. ticket -> INC-5991
Maya: locking thread and moving follow-ups to #postmortems once we have the writeup.
